title: Digital transformation is increasingly governed as an investment, infrastructure, and public-capability problem rather than a technology-adoption problem alone
source_unit: OECD, Investment Policy Framework for Digital Transformation
geography: OECD policy and investment context, with country examples from Morocco, Uzbekistan, and Viet Nam

denominator.unit: OECD investment-policy framework and cross-policy diagnostic universe

framework_building_blocks.value: governance; regulatory framework; technical and financial support; information and facilitation

policy_domains.value: investment, competition, cross-border data flows, trade and investment agreements, skills, and responsible business conduct

objective.value: mobilise more, better, and safer international investment that supports digital transformation

observations.method: OECD policy framework synthesizing OECD investment tools, cross-cutting digital frameworks, policy questions, and country examples to diagnose gaps and opportunities for investment supporting digital transformation.
observations.uncertainty: This is a normative and diagnostic framework, not a cross-country estimate of investment effects, digital adoption, productivity, employment, or public-service quality. The four building blocks are organizing concepts, not evidence that each has equal importance in every country.
observations.subgroup: Governments, investment-promotion agencies, regulators, domestic and foreign firms, workers, skills systems, data-governance institutions, and communities affected by digital infrastructure and services.
observations.counterinterpretation: Attracting international investment can increase capability and connectivity, but may also create dependency, concentration, data-control, tax, labour, or local-impact risks when competition, standards, skills, and accountability are weak.

observations.period: 2026 framework; international investment and domestic digital capability

denominator.unit: OECD framework's country-assessment and policy-instrument comparison frame

country_examples.value: Morocco, Uzbekistan, and Viet Nam are used as concrete country examples in mapping policies and institutions and in-depth assessments

investment_capability_route.value: strategic direction, coherent regulation, technical and financial support, information, and administrative facilitation are treated as conditions for quality digital investment

quality_dimension.value: digital investment should be assessed by its contribution to inclusive transformation, not only by capital volume or attraction

observations.method: OECD framework grounded in the FDI Qualities Initiative, FDI Regulatory Restrictiveness Index, Investment Tax Incentives Database, Mapping of Investment Promotion Agencies, and country-policy assessments.
observations.uncertainty: The source identifies policy levers and examples but does not provide a common outcome measure across the three countries or prove that a given investment-policy reform caused better distribution, resilience, jobs, or state leverage.
observations.subgroup: Countries and regions seeking digital investment, firms choosing locations and suppliers, public agencies coordinating investment and digital policy, and workers or communities affected by investment quality.
observations.counterinterpretation: A coherent investment framework may still fail where implementation capacity, electricity and connectivity, skills, local ownership, labour standards, or public bargaining power are inadequate; policy coherence is not realized capability.

related_sources.claim: Persistent OECD identifier for the framework.
Related OECD whole-of-government digital-policy framework covering access, jobs, trust, society, and market openness.

boundary: This record adds an investment-governance and digital-capability route distinct from the OECD digital-government AI-adoption record. It is not firm-level investment data, does not estimate local infrastructure or household effects, and does not establish that foreign investment produces digital inclusion, worker power, public-service improvement, or geopolitical leverage.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official OECD full-report page and metadata were retrieved; title, publication date, four building blocks, cross-domain policy set, country examples, and source tools were cross-checked. The hash is a source-URL fingerprint because the OECD host rejected automated HTML/PDF retrieval.
